ws1.gap_parameter_growth: Kosh passed to a prakriya that grows it (grow(kosh k) { kosh_kship(k, ...) }; caller reads kk) COMPILE-refuses: 'Sutram truti: kosh-tarke kosh_push asamarthitam' (kosh_push unsupported for kosh parameters). Diagnostic nit: message says kosh_push (old name) even though the program used kosh_kship (current name) - message should say kosh_kship. This is the most significant gap found: descriptor design does not support growing a kosh inside a callee (parameters are shared for reading, but growth via parameters is unsupported, likely because parameters are passed by value (copy of the descriptor) so growth would update the copy, not the caller's descriptor, leading to a stale caller descriptor - so v302 refuses it rather than allowing stale). If 'defect' means crash/silent wrong, this is NOT one (it refuses safely). If 'defect' includes design gaps (refused patterns that should work), this IS the ninth/tenth. Whether parameter growth should be supported (by passing descriptors by reference, or by updating the caller's descriptor on growth) is the owner's/Claude's design decision.

ws1.oom: Push 20M elements into a kosh under ulimit -v 65536 (64 MB): message, not crash - 'Sutram truti: kosh vardhayitum smritih na labdha - kosh yatha asit tatha eva' (kosh growth: memory not obtained - kosh remains as it was), exit 1 (confirmed without pipes, 1 line, no segfault). Works - OOM is a message (exit 1, clean abort, not SIGSEGV), as claimed. Without the ulimit, 20M pushes succeed (160 MB), exit 0, k[0]=0 - so OOM only triggers when memory is actually exhausted, not spuriously.

ws2.twenty_k_one_mmap: Program ws2_20k_maps.sm: create 20,000 koshes via make_kosh() + global counter, then pause at grahan() (waits for input) while inspecting /proc/<pid>/maps and /proc/<pid>/status, then send newline to finish. Result while paused (20,000 koshes live): 8 mappings total, 1 large (>=16 MB) mapping of exactly 1024 MB (1 GiB arena, one mmap, shared for all kosh buffers, not per-kosh regions), VmSize: 1048816 kB (~1,024 MB + binary/stack overhead), VmRSS: 1276 kB (~1.2 MB, only touched pages, lazy). Final output after resume: 'ready' + last[0]=19999 (correct, 20,000th kosh), exit 0. So: 20,000 koshes work, they use ONE mmap (1 GiB arena, shared), not 20,000 x 64 MB regions (which would have been 20,000 mappings, ~1.28 TB VSZ, and would have crashed at the 16th under a 1 GiB limit on v300). The 64 MiB per-kosh region is GONE (replaced by one shared arena + 24-byte descriptors), and RSS stays tiny (1.2 MB, lazy) despite 20,000 live koshes. Headline VERIFIED.
